script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

Title:
Fight for Glory

Genre: Sports
Logline:
When a promising mixed martial artist is forced to retire due to a career-ending injury, he finds solace in the world of wheelchair basketball and discovers an unexpected path to redemption.

INT. GYM - DAY

(A packed gym. Sweat drips from the ceiling. Scores of people train in various sports. Our PROTAGONIST, MIKE, moves with a graceful agility. He throws punches and kicks, his sweat-streaked face focused and determined.)

MIKE
(Talking to himself)
I'll be back. I'll come back stronger than ever.

INT. MIKE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

(Mike sits alone in his small, cluttered apartment. His girlfriend, AMELIA, enters. She holds a bouquet of flowers and looks worried.)

AMELIA
(Concerned)
Mike, how are you feeling today?

MIKE
(Sighs)
I don't know, Amelia. The doctor said it's going to be a long road to recovery. I don't know if I have it in me.

AMELIA
(Comfortingly)
You have me, and you have all of us. We'll get through this together.

INT. REHAB CENTER - DAY

(Mike undergoes intense physical therapy sessions. His PT, OLIVIA, motivates him as he struggles to regain his strength.)

OLIVIA
(Encouragingly)
You're stronger than you think, Mike. You've got this.

INT. GYM - DAY

(Mike watches from the sidelines as a group of wheelchair basketball players practice. He's intrigued and approaches them.)

MIKE
(Curiously)
What's this sport called? Wheelchair basketball?

PLAYER 1
(Laughs)
That's right! And you're never too old or too injured to play.

INT. MIKE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

(Mike tells Amelia about his new discovery and the potential for a new career in wheelchair basketball.)

AMELIA
(Supportively)
You should give it a try, Mike. It might be just what you need.

EXT. REHAB CENTER PARKING LOT - DAY

(Mike pushes his wheelchair out of the rehab center, determined to join the team. Olivia meets him outside and gives him a warm smile.)

OLIVIA
(Encouragingly)
You've got this, Mike.

INT. GYM - DAY

(Mike struggles at first, but with the help of his new teammates and his own determination, he begins to excel at wheelchair basketball. He scores a game-winning shot in a friendly scrimmage, earning cheers and praise from his teammates.)

MIKE
(Excitedly)
I think I might just have a future in this sport after all.

INT. TRAINING ROOM - NIGHT

(Mike trains diligently, both physically and mentally, pushing himself to be the best wheelchair basketball player he can be. Amelia supports him every step of the way.)

INT. COMPETITION VENUE - DAY

(Mike and his team compete in a wheelchair basketball tournament. They face off against a formidable rival team, but Mike's determination and skills shine through. They win the tournament, and Mike is crowned MVP.)

AMELIA
(Proudly)
You did it, Mike. You proved to everyone that no matter what life throws at you, you can always find a way to fight for glory.

Fade to black.

THE END.
